item.title: “ICE Out” Pins Are All Over New York Fashion Week and the Red Carpets—What’s Next?
item.description: “If American fashion wants credibility, it must stop treating immigration as a trend and start defending the people who make the industry exist,” says Mexican designer Patricio Campillo, who appeared after his runway show wearing an ICE Out pin.

item.title: Evie Magazine’s Brittany Hugoboom Wants Women to Have It All (With Some Caveats for Vaccines, Hormones, and Abortions)
item.description: The 34-year-old editor in chief of the glossy guide for the women with paradoxical politics wants to blend the liberal health world with a conservative relationship world.

item.title: Casting Directors Hate the Spotlight—but for the Oscars, They’ll Make an Exception
item.description: As the Academy Awards prepare to honor them with their very own category, the industry’s foremost ensemble-wranglers reflect on what this moment means—and hope it’ll shed some light on their misunderstood, oft-overlooked profession.

item.title: The One Question Tyra Banks Refused to Answer in the America’s Next Top Model Documentary
item.description: The real-life couple behind Netflix’s viral docuseries on Banks’s rare four-hour interview, their personal connection to the project, and why “some form of America Next Top Model is happening every day on TikTok.”

item.title: Inside Bunny Mellon’s New York Home, Immortalized in Watercolor
item.description: As the Mellon family’s live-in artist, Snowy Campbell captured the colors and atmosphere of the Mellons’ many homes. Now, in a new book, her enchanting paintings are published for the first time.

item.title: Trump’s Wild West Wing Pardons: Inside the Absolutions of Todd Chrisley, Carlos Watson, Sidney Powell, and Other Boldface Pardonees
item.description: Willem Marx speaks to pardoners, pardonees, and the as-yet-unpardoned, from a Bush-era CIA leaker struggling for salvation to reality TV’s favorite criminal couple.

item.title: George, JFK Jr.’s Real Magazine From Love Story, Ended in Failure. Its Photo Shoots Were Legendary.
item.description: George art director Matt Berman remembers the first son’s dedication to the publication, and the cover photo he absolutely refused to pose for with Carolyn Bessette: “He said, ‘Come on, I’m not gonna whore out myself and my wife for the magazine!’”

item.title: A Day in the Life of Jenni Kayne, California’s Favorite Cashmere-Wearing Lifestyle Guru
item.description: Jenni Kayne built a 140 million dollar business selling sweaters, boucle chairs, and clean skincare to Brentwood moms and then some. Here's how she lives the very life she monetized.

item.title: Exclusive: OpenAI Has Poached Instagram’s Celebrity Whisperer
item.description: Charles Porch’s newly created role as OpenAI’s VP of global creative partnerships signals the AI giant’s new focus on the entertainment industry

item.title: Dylan Mulvaney Is Finally a Broadway Leading Lady, Haters Be Damned
item.description: The social media star opens up about her Broadway debut in the Tony-winning musical Six, her goals for dating in NYC, and all the Bud Light drama she survived to get here.
